newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends near low posted in late trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends near low posted in late trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude lost ground to close near session lows on Monday after failing to consolidate early Iraq-inspired gains as weak U.S. heating oil continued to undermine sentiment, brokers said.

The U.S. Defence Department said a U.S. fighter fired a missle at an Iraqi anti-aircraft system on Monday, the second such incident in three days. Baghdad decribed the Pentagon statement as "groundless fabrication".
"It tried to bounce on the news earlier in the day but since then it's just been adding volume at the lower end of the range," said a broker.
IPE Dec Brent closed down 25 cents at $22.25 a barrel, just five cents above the session low posted in late trade and 45 cents off the high revisited in the wake of the Iraq reports.
Brokers said weak U.S. heating oil, which until mid-October was the main market motor, continued to undermine sentiment ahead of the latest weekly U.S. stocks data due to be released on Tuesday.
"Unless we see a sizeable draw it will just confirm the recent trend," said a broker.
"Another big build in U.S. heating oil stocks and we could test $200 (on prompt gas oil)," said another.

Dealers said sloppy physical crude markets were also weighing on Brent, pressure which intensified when the U.S. government set a deadline of 1800 GMT Thursday for bids to be submitted in the final round of its sale of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
"There appears to be plenty of North Sea crude around so the market doesn't need any more," said a broker.
Earlier, Nov IPE gas oil fell $3.00 to close at $209.00 a tonne while Dec finished just $1.75 lower at $205.25.
